definitions.constraint_defined_identity: An object is identified not only by its fields but by the closure of required positive relations, forbidden relations, types, cardinalities and invariants.
definitions.magic_key: A minimal constraint subset that still uniquely discriminates one intended object/state from all registered alternatives under a frozen comparison universe.
definitions.semantic_collision: Two distinct intended meanings or states that satisfy the same frozen structural/constraint key.
definitions.role_swap: A controlled transformation in which data becomes constraints/schema and constraints/schema generate candidate data, followed by round-trip comparison.
definitions.meta_object: A JSON artifact that carries observations about itself, its schema, provenance and permissible interpreter behavior without executing itself.

conceptual_seed.use: structural only; no theological truth claim
conceptual_seed.structural_lesson: Identity can be constrained by simultaneous positive and negative edges; removing either class can collapse distinctions.
conceptual_seed.translation_to_json: Represent object identity as a constraint graph rather than as a flat bag of labels.

hypotheses.claim: For some JSON domains, identity is more robustly recoverable from the closure of positive+negative constraints than from any single identifier field.
hypotheses.falsifier: A frozen benchmark where identifiers alone match or exceed constraint closure on recovery under field deletion, reordering and aliasing.

hypotheses.claim: A smallest or near-smallest distinguishing constraint subgraph can function as a compact semantic key for a registered universe.
hypotheses.falsifier: No stable minimal/near-minimal discriminator exists across held-out perturbations, or keys are so universe-specific that they fail immediately out of sample.

hypotheses.claim: Selected JSON fragments can alternate between instance-data and constraint roles while preserving useful invariants across a controlled round trip.
hypotheses.falsifier: Role swaps systematically destroy type/semantic invariants or require human retuning to reconstruct the original.

hypotheses.claim: A constraint-key can be evaluated for semantic collision resistance independently from cryptographic hash collision resistance.
hypotheses.falsifier: Semantic collisions cannot be operationally defined or measured without changing the frozen meaning labels after results are seen.

hypotheses.claim: Dataset, schema declaration, provenance, tests and declarative state-machine instructions can coexist in one JSON artifact without becoming unsafe executable code.
hypotheses.falsifier: Interpreters cannot preserve a strict capability boundary, or the combined artifact becomes materially less auditable than separated files.

hypotheses.claim: A constrained JSON subset can be projected to an explicit labeled graph and back with canonical semantic equivalence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Round-trip loses distinctions required by the frozen canonical semantics or produces non-deterministic reconstructions.

hypotheses.claim: A JSON record can represent nested observer→subject→observer relations while keeping provenance and authority separable at every layer.
hypotheses.falsifier: Nested observer records produce unavoidable authority leakage or ambiguous provenance under the frozen interpreter.

hypotheses.claim: Behavior may be safely unlocked by satisfying a structural invariant set rather than by a secret token, when the behavior is declarative and capability-limited.
hypotheses.falsifier: Equivalent malformed or adversarial structures satisfy the gate, or key satisfaction depends on parser-specific quirks.

novelty_boundary: These are research hypotheses and synthesis candidates. 'Nobody has noticed this before' is not asserted without an external prior-art review.
